findings: Remediation control VEAP-PRIV-CONTROL-001-V0.2 explicitly binds purpose classes (EXECUTION_ACCOUNTABILITY, EVIDENCE_VERIFICATION, GOVERNANCE_REVIEW) and recipient classes (SUBJECT_OWNER, AUTHORIZED_VERIFIER, AUTHORIZED_GOVERNANCE_REVIEWER).

Secondary use default is set to FORBIDDEN with a requirement for SEPARATE_EXPLICIT_DECISION_REFERENCE, directly addressing the risk of execution evidence reuse for surveillance, profiling, or unrelated decisions.
Stop condition PURPOSE_OR_RECIPIENT_CLASS_MISSING_OR_SECONDARY_USE_DECISION_ABSENT is defined and not triggered by the supplied control profile.
residual_risks: Enforcement of secondary use prohibition depends on runtime governance mechanisms not evidenced in the supplied control profile.
Recipient class boundaries (e.g., AUTHORIZED_VERIFIER scope) require external authorization definitions not present in the reviewed artifacts.

findings: Remediation control VEAP-PRIV-CONTROL-002-V0.2 enforces REFERENCE_FIRST_RAW_CONTENT_FORBIDDEN as the exchange default, directly mitigating unnecessary collection of prompt, response, or tool content.
Field authorization table maps seven field categories to specific purposes and authority scopes, satisfying the field-level purpose and authorization requirement.
Raw content requirements include SEPARATE_CONTENT_AUTHORIZATION_REFERENCE, EXPLICIT_FIELD_ALLOWLIST, REDACTION, and SECRET_SCAN, providing layered minimization controls.
Stop condition FIELD_JUSTIFICATION_OR_RAW_CONTENT_AUTHORIZATION_MISSING is defined and not triggered.
residual_risks: Completeness goals at the system level may still drive collection pressure; the control profile defines defaults but does not evidence systemic enforcement against scope creep.
Field-level authorization depends on external authority scope definitions (e.g., AUTHORIZED_SUBJECT_SCOPE) not included in the reviewed artifacts.

findings: Remediation control VEAP-PRIV-CONTROL-003-V0.2 defines four retention classes (REFERENCE_ONLY, RESTRICTED_REFERENCE, PUBLIC_SAFE_EXTRACT, CONTENT_AUTHORIZED) supporting class-based retention.

Requirements include RETENTION_POLICY_REFERENCE, CONTENT_FREE_TOMBSTONE, DELETION_PROOF_REFERENCE, and SEPARATE_LEGAL_HOLD_REFERENCE, addressing tombstone/revocation, deletion proof, and legal-hold boundary.
Immutable history boundary is explicitly set to PRESERVE_PERMITTED_REFERENCE_OR_TOMBSTONE_LINEAGE_NOT_DELETED_CONTENT, reconciling retention/deletion duties with immutability constraints.
Stop condition RETENTION_POLICY_OR_DELETION_PROOF_OR_LEGAL_HOLD_BOUNDARY_MISSING is defined and not triggered.
residual_risks: Withdrawal duties requiring active revocation of previously permitted references depend on runtime mechanisms not evidenced in the control profile.
Legal-hold boundary definition references external legal processes; the control profile provides a reference placeholder but not operational legal-hold procedures.

findings: Remediation control VEAP-PRIV-CONTROL-004-V0.2 requires SOURCE_NAMESPACE_BINDING, TARGET_NAMESPACE_BINDING, ACCESS_SCOPE, and LINKABILITY_ASSESSMENT_REFERENCE, directly addressing linkability review and namespace separation.
Public safe extract rule CORRELATING_IDENTIFIERS_FORBIDDEN explicitly prohibits correlating identifiers in public-safe extractions, mitigating re-identification risk.
Stop condition NAMESPACE_SEPARATION_OR_LINKABILITY_ASSESSMENT_MISSING is defined and not triggered.
residual_risks: Linkability assessment reference implies an external assessment artifact; the control profile does not evidence completion of such an assessment.
Access scope definitions for namespace bindings depend on external authorization frameworks not included in the reviewed artifacts.

limitations: This review is advisory and source-bound; it does not constitute a human decision, authority grant, risk acceptance, or Gate PASS.

Control sufficiency assessments are based solely on the structural completeness of the supplied remediation control profiles against stated risk requirements; operational effectiveness is not evaluated.
External authorization scope definitions, runtime enforcement mechanisms, and legal-hold procedures referenced by the control profiles are not included in the reviewed artifacts.
Evidence is not truth; evaluation is not authority; recommendation is not decision; decision is not execution; capability is not permission.
